title: Multimodal fallback UX idea journal
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick brain dump for a product-facing UX around multimodal requests (images/audio/video) when the requested endpoint/model doesn't support the modality, or the server wants to route to a specialized model variant (cheaper, higher-fidelity, or on-prem).
- Goal: make behavior predictable for developers + end-users; surface choices, costs and graceful degradations.

Problem statements / why this matters:
- Hosted API currently returns 400/unsupported-model for image/audio inputs if a text-only model is called — leads to brittle client logic and poor developer experience.
- Clients often do not know which model supports which modality; they pick a default text model and then get errors.
- For apps mixing modalities (e.g., chat + image), we need consistent UX for: fallback routing, cost transparency, latency expectations, and privacy constraints (e.g., image must stay on-prem).

Top-level ideas (brainstorm):
1) Autonomous fallback routing: server can detect modality and transparently route to a compatible model variant (e.g., multimodal-1, image-caption-2). Client gets a header/metadata in response explaining the routing decision and cost delta.
2) Opt-in explicit fallback: client supplies fallback policy in request ("fallback": "auto|ask|reject") and optional max-cost delta.
3) Interactive negotiation: for long-running flows, send a preflight (HEAD-like) response indicating model choices, estimated latency & cost, then proceed on explicit OK. (useful for mobile UX)
4) Graceful degradation responses: when image input can't be processed, return a structured response summarizing why + suggested next steps (e.g., "try compressing image", "send text-only prompt").
5) On-prem aware routing: if customer has private deployment with "restrict_images": true, server respects that and rejects or routes to private model.

User stories (rough):
- As a developer, I want the API to auto-route an image upload to a multimodal model so my client code can be simpler.
- As a compliance officer, I want image data to never leave a private deployment, even if a hosted multimodal model would be cheaper.
- As a product designer, I want to explain to users when we used a different model for an image and show a short rationale if output quality changes.
- As an ops engineer, I want telemetry events for every fallback decision (why, from which model to which) so we can monitor increased cost or error surface.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- API accepts mixed-modality input and, when fallback policy is "auto", returns a 2xx response for >95% of valid inputs (previously many returned 4xx).
- Fallback routing events appear in Console with breakdown: count, avg latency delta, avg cost delta, top reasons.
- End-to-end latency increase for auto-fallback flows <= 1.5x baseline for same-size text-only requests (target).
- No private-deployment image is routed out-of-region when "restrict_images" flag is set (policy enforced).

Telemetry / observability hooks (notes):
- Request metadata: original_model, chosen_model, fallback_reason (unsupported_modality|capacity|cost_policy|private_restriction), estimated_cost_delta, estimated_latency_delta, region_hint.
- Console: per-customer badge showing % of requests that used fallback last 7/30/90 days.
- Evals: spot-check outputs pre/post fallback to detect hallucination regressions when using specialized models.

API design sketches (fields to add):
- client_fallback_policy: "auto|ask|reject" (default auto)
- fallback_constraints: {"max_cost_multiplier": "1.3", "allow_external_routing": "false"}  <-- note: data stored as structured JSON string in request metadata (we'll spec shape later)
- preflight=true => return potential routing choices and costs without consuming user quota (consumes a cheap preflight token).

UX flows (developer + end-user):
1) Simple auto flow: developer sets fallback=auto, client posts image+prompt -> server routes -> response includes x-redwood-routing header and routing explanation in metadata.
2) Preflight flow: mobile client calls preflight to show "cost: +$0.02, latency: +300ms" modal, user confirms, then main call.
3) Ask flow: API responds with code 300-FALLBACK-OPTIONS and a small JSON describing options; client can choose. Useful for web apps wanting explicit consent for paid upgrades.

Privacy/security constraints:
- Must enforce org-level policy: allow_external_routing (boolean) or allow_multimodal (boolean). Default: true for hosted accounts, false for enterprise private deployments.
- Ensure audit logs record any time data crosses deployment boundary.

Prototype plan (MVP):
- Minimal server change: routing table + fallback_reason tagging (2 backend PRs: routing + metadata).
- API extension: add simple client_fallback_policy enum + return header explaining chosen_model.
- Console: add fallback-events view (counts + basic cost delta) — quick chart.
- UX: small modal prototype for preflight confirmation (design by Sophia).
- Timeline: 4 sprints for MVP (routing infra + API extension + basic console).

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- How do we charge for preflight? free? cheap token? risk: abuse.
- Backwards compatibility: what should default be for older SDKs? keep as-is (reject unsupported) or set to auto? prefer keep-as-is to avoid surprise charges.
- How to represent cost estimate: token-based delta vs flat multiplier? need product input.
- Do we allow multi-step fallbacks (image -> caption model -> text model) and attribution of which model produced which piece? complexity high.
- Need SRE input on capacity signals: if routing due to capacity constraints, should we degrade quality or queue?

Implementation notes (dev ops):
- Add routing metrics to existing poison-pill: tag traces with fallback_reason for easy tracing.
- Add unit tests: routing table behavior, policy precedence (request-level > org-level > account default).
- Add e2e tests with mocked private deployment to ensure no cross-boundary routing.

Communication / rollout plan:
- Beta to selected customers (Enterprise with multimodal needs) behind feature flag.
- SDK update: v0.14 client_fallback_policy support + header parsing.
- Changelog entry + migration guide (default behavior, how to opt-in/out).

References / links (notes):
- Slack thread: #prod-multimodal (see thread t12345)
- Related Jira: JIRA-INF-9214 (routing infra), JIRA-INF-9398 (console changes)

Rough parking-lot ideas for follow-ups:
- "Fallback explainability": short natural-language rationale returned to end-user explaining model swap.
- UX A/B test: auto vs ask on conversion/engagement and user trust metrics.
- Bandwidth-conscious preflight: send compressed image features to estimate cost without full upload (edge case).

Closing random notes to self:
- Keep default conservative (reject) to avoid surprising costs.
- Make telemetry first-class — we need to show customers value (reduced errors, cost tradeoffs).
- Chat with Miguel about model attribution UI (who owns the caption if we stitched models?).
- Trigger: sync with Compliance next week (Mar 4) to validate private deploy constraints.

-- end of scratchpad --
